title: Projection queue claim/finish/recovery measurement (synthetic, PostgreSQL 14)

environment.fixture: per-run scratch database from the schema plus synthetic rows; 1k/10k/100k links (IMAP/OUTLOOK/GMAIL mix), two hot mailboxes with 20,002 outbox rows each; dropped after each run

statistics.stale: ANALYZE of a tiny seed, autovacuum off, then the full seed

measurementMethod: Each claim runs the source prelude and both statements (lock_projection_window, claim_locked_projection) in one READ COMMITTED transaction.

EXPLAIN-sampled claims add a helper-only replay of lock_projection_window in the same transaction to read the ids; it re-selects the 64 rows the transaction already holds, takes no new locks and writes nothing.

Reported buffers (shared hit+read), row locks (LockRows rows x loops) and execution ms are the sum of the two source plans only; the replay and harness bookkeeping are excluded. No figure is a whole-transaction wall time.

Unsampled full-drain calls run the window and core once each; their client ms are round-trips around the source statements only. Row-change counts are pg_stat_xact_user_tables deltas around the source statements.
Heavy scenario states are committed and vacuumed before measuring, then restored.

gate.kind: approved benchmark criterion for this synthetic measurement, not a production measurement
history: Original criterion <=3000 buffers per claim transaction: missed by 13 matrix cells (FIFO backoff, leased and locked-uncommitted cases; worst 3,304).
Conditional <=3500 criterion: missed by FIFO backoff at 100k links with stale statistics, generic plan (3,571; custom 3,461) in the same-data stage comparison.
The criterion was then split by vacuum state after the per-stage review: the stale-statistics excess comes from the head probe visiting heap pages while the visibility map is unset.

stageAttributionSameData.stages: window = lock_projection_window (v3: due CTE); reread = statement-2 primary-key reread of the locked ids; head = link_fifo head probe; links; inactive; deferred; claimed
findings: The increase over v3 on the same data is the statement-2 primary-key reread of the 64 locked ids (269 buffers at 1k, ~370 at 10k, 383-407 at 100k): 64 x (index depth + heap).
Miss of the restated <=3500: FIFO backoff, 100k links, stale statistics, generic plan = 3,571 (custom 3,461); v3 on the same data and plan = 3,172 (custom 3,004).
The head probe costs 257-296 buffers with fresh statistics but 381-644 in the stale build (visibility map unset), growing with not-all-visible pages rather than link count.
The deferred UPDATE (64 non-HOT updates into every index) is the largest stage in both versions (1,540-1,934 buffers).
A 90% parked share costs the same as the ordinary case.

notes: Each normal finish writes 2 rows: the delete and the transaction-1 successor wake; the guarded transaction-2 wake updates 0 rows (no HOT updates over the drain); the final finish (no successor) writes 1.

Guarded wake plan at every sample: Limit -> LockRows -> Index Scan on email_projection_outbox_link_fifo (successor, 1 row), CTE Scan with Filter (blocked_until IS NOT NULL), Index Scan on email_projection_outbox_pkey; transaction 2 filters the successor out (0 rows) unless a claimer deferred it.

With autovacuum off, the claim core head probe and both wake lookups grow linearly with dead deleted heads (about +13 buffers per 1,000; tx1 wake 31-33 -> ~290, tx2 wake 5-6 -> ~263); the lock window stays flat and the advisory locks read no buffers.
Finish client ms are round-trips around the source statements of both finish transactions.

discoveryFallback.summary: Index Only Scan on email_links_pkey returning 1 row (0 past the last id), 2-4 buffers at every size, statistics and plan mode.

priorM3RecoveryWalk.receipt: prior M3 recovery walk (per-probe COMMIT + halving retry loop); its known-link unpark and sweep statements are identical in the final source, which adds only the N4 parent-PK discovery fallback

wraps.wrap: locked: 10 active links with all parked rows row-locked
slow link: 5 ms per row (64-row unpark > 250 ms)

notes: slow-link wrap uses a scratch-only BEFORE UPDATE trigger sleeping 5 ms per row on one link so a 64-row unpark exceeds the 250 ms probe timeout
the locked wrap holds row locks in a second open transaction; its higher page cost reflects dead entries that cannot be cleaned while that transaction holds the horizon
worker consecutive-skip accounting is Rust in-memory and was not emulated

finishShape: finish_projection: transaction 1 takes the namespaced per-link finish lock, records the fenced outcome (delete, or release with retry) and wakes exactly the successor if it is still blocked; after commit, transaction 2 (best effort) takes the same lock and repeats the guarded wake, which only writes when a claimer deferred the successor while transaction 1 was open.

n6PostCommitWakeInterleave.scenario: transaction 1 locks, deletes the head and finds no successor (0 rows), then pauses; a producer commits successor S; a real claimer, seeing the still-visible head, defers S by 1-2 h; transaction 1 commits with S still blocked; transaction 2 locks and its guarded wake clears S (1 row); the next claim acquires S.

history: Earlier drain receipts counted 2 rows per finish with a single-transaction finish, then 3 rows per finish with an unguarded post-commit wake; both are superseded by the guarded two-transaction finish measured here.
